import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Quantum unique ergodicity for eigenfunctions of the Laplacian

The quantum unique ergodicity (QUE) conjecture of Rudnick and Sarnak concerns the distribution of
large-frequency eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on a compact Riemannian manifold
$M$ without boundary with strictly negative sectional curvature. It asserts that for *every*
sequence $(\varphi_k)$ of $L^2$-normalised eigenfunctions, $\Delta \varphi_k = \lambda_k \varphi_k$
with $\lambda_k \to \infty$, the probability measures $|\varphi_k|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}$ converge
weakly to the normalised Riemannian volume $d\mathrm{vol} / \mathrm{vol}(M)$. This strengthens the
quantum ergodicity theorem of Shnirelman, Zelditch and Colin de Verdière, which gives this
conclusion only along a subsequence of density one.

This file states the conjecture on the manifold $M$ itself (convergence of the measures
$|\varphi_k|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}$). The phase-space version, that Liouville measure is the only
quantum limit of the microlocal lifts on the unit cotangent bundle, is stronger and is not stated
here.

Mathlib has Riemannian manifolds (`IsRiemannianManifold`), but no Laplace–Beltrami operator,
Riemannian volume measure or curvature tensor. This file defines these notions from existing
primitives:

* the Riemannian volume is realised as the `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the Riemannian
  distance (`n = dim M`), which is a positive constant multiple of the Riemannian volume; the
  constant disappears after normalisation;
* eigenfunctions of the Laplacian are defined through the weak form of the eigenvalue equation
  $\int_M \langle \nabla \varphi, \nabla \psi \rangle = \lambda \int_M \varphi \psi$ for all smooth
  $\psi$, which on a compact manifold without boundary is equivalent to
  $\Delta \varphi = \lambda \varphi$ for the non-negative Laplacian
  $\Delta = -\operatorname{div} \nabla$;
* the sectional curvature is computed from the Christoffel symbols of the metric coefficients in
  the preferred chart at each point.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Eigenfunction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/eigenfunction)
* [Wikipedia, Quantum ergodicity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_ergodicity)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [RS94] Z. Rudnick, P. Sarnak, *The behaviour of eigenstates of arithmetic hyperbolic
  manifolds*, Comm. Math. Phys. 161 (1994), 195–213.
* [Sa11] P. Sarnak, *Recent progress on the quantum unique ergodicity conjecture*,
  Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 48 (2011), 211–228.
-/
open Bundle MeasureTheory Filter Topology
open scoped Manifold ContDiff
namespace Eigenfunction

/-
Throughout, `M` is a Riemannian manifold modelled on a finite-dimensional real vector space `E`:
its tangent spaces carry inner products (`RiemannianBundle`), and its extended distance is the
Riemannian distance (`IsRiemannianManifold I M`).
-/

variable
  {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  {H : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H)
  {M : Type*} [EMetricSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
  [RiemannianBundle (fun (x : M) ↦ TangentSpace I x)]

blocks.command_arg: "⟪" x ", " y "⟫" => inner ℝ x y
blocks.text: local notation "⟪" x ", " y "⟫" => inner ℝ x y

/- ### Riemannian volume and the Laplace–Beltrami operator -/

blocks.code:
noncomputable def normalizedVolume (M : Type*) [EMetricSpace M] [MeasurableSpace M]
    [BorelSpace M] (n : ℕ) : Measure M :=
  (μH[n] (Set.univ : Set M))⁻¹ • μH[n]
blocks.docstring:
The normalised `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of an extended metric space `M`.

When `M` is a compact `n`-dimensional Riemannian manifold whose distance is the Riemannian
distance, the `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure is a positive constant multiple of the
Riemannian volume, so `normalizedVolume M n` is the normalised Riemannian volume
$d\mathrm{vol} / \mathrm{vol}(M)$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure (μH[d]) — used as the building block; no Riemannian volume form/measure exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
justification.name: Eigenfunction.normalizedVolume
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no Riemannian volume measure on manifolds. The normalised n-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the Riemannian distance equals the normalised Riemannian volume.

blocks.name: normalizedVolume
blocks.text:
/-- The normalised `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of an extended metric space `M`.

When `M` is a compact `n`-dimensional Riemannian manifold whose distance is the Riemannian
distance, the `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure is a positive constant multiple of the
Riemannian volume, so `normalizedVolume M n` is the normalised Riemannian volume
$d\mathrm{vol} / \mathrm{vol}(M)$. -/
noncomputable def normalizedVolume (M : Type*) [EMetricSpace M] [MeasurableSpace M]
    [BorelSpace M] (n : ℕ) : Measure M :=
  (μH[n] (Set.univ : Set M))⁻¹ • μH[n]

blocks.code:
noncomputable def gradient (φ : M → ℝ) (x : M) : TangentSpace I x :=
  (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (TangentSpace I x)).symm (mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) φ x)
blocks.docstring:
The Riemannian gradient of a function `φ : M → ℝ` at `x`: the tangent vector at `x`
representing the differential `dφ_x` through the Riemannian inner product on `TangentSpace I x`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: mfderiv and InnerProductSpace.toDual (combined); Mathlib's `gradient` only exists for functions on inner product spaces, not on manifolds.
justification.name: Eigenfunction.gradient
justification.why_needed: Riemannian gradient of a real function, needed for the weak form of the Laplace eigenvalue equation.

blocks.name: gradient
blocks.text:
/-- The Riemannian gradient of a function `φ : M → ℝ` at `x`: the tangent vector at `x`
representing the differential `dφ_x` through the Riemannian inner product on `TangentSpace I x`.
-/
noncomputable def gradient (φ : M → ℝ) (x : M) : TangentSpace I x :=
  (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (TangentSpace I x)).symm (mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) φ x)

blocks.code:
def IsLaplaceEigenfunction [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M] (φ : M → ℝ) (l : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ φ ∧ ∀ ψ : M → ℝ, ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ ψ →
    ∫ x, ⟪gradient I φ x, gradient I ψ x⟫ ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E)) =
      l * ∫ x, φ x * ψ x ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E))
blocks.docstring:
`IsLaplaceEigenfunction I φ l` means that `φ : M → ℝ` is a smooth eigenfunction of the
Laplace–Beltrami operator with eigenvalue `l`, in weak form: for every smooth `ψ : M → ℝ`,
$$\int_M \langle \nabla \varphi, \nabla \psi \rangle \, d\mathrm{vol}
  = l \int_M \varphi \, \psi \, d\mathrm{vol}.$$
On a compact manifold without boundary, Green's formula shows that this is equivalent to
$\Delta \varphi = l \varphi$ for the non-negative Laplace–Beltrami operator
$\Delta = -\operatorname{div} \nabla$. Eigenfunctions of the Laplacian are smooth by elliptic
regularity, so requiring `φ` to be smooth loses no generality.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `Laplacian`/`Δ` (InnerProductSpace.Laplacian) is only for functions on inner product spaces (used e.g. in Paper/DeGiorgi.lean and Millenium/NavierStokes.lean), not on manifolds.
justification.name: Eigenfunction.IsLaplaceEigenfunction
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no Laplace–Beltrami operator on Riemannian manifolds; the weak formulation via gradients is equivalent to Δφ = λφ on a closed manifold.

blocks.name: IsLaplaceEigenfunction
blocks.text:
/-- `IsLaplaceEigenfunction I φ l` means that `φ : M → ℝ` is a smooth eigenfunction of the
Laplace–Beltrami operator with eigenvalue `l`, in weak form: for every smooth `ψ : M → ℝ`,
$$\int_M \langle \nabla \varphi, \nabla \psi \rangle \, d\mathrm{vol}
  = l \int_M \varphi \, \psi \, d\mathrm{vol}.$$
On a compact manifold without boundary, Green's formula shows that this is equivalent to
$\Delta \varphi = l \varphi$ for the non-negative Laplace–Beltrami operator
$\Delta = -\operatorname{div} \nabla$. Eigenfunctions of the Laplacian are smooth by elliptic
regularity, so requiring `φ` to be smooth loses no generality. -/
def IsLaplaceEigenfunction [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M] (φ : M → ℝ) (l : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ φ ∧ ∀ ψ : M → ℝ, ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ ψ →
    ∫ x, ⟪gradient I φ x, gradient I ψ x⟫ ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E)) =
      l * ∫ x, φ x * ψ x ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E))

/-
### Sectional curvature

The curvature at a point `x₀` is computed in the preferred chart `e = extChartAt I x₀`. A vector
`v : E` is identified with the coordinate vector field `y ↦ D(e⁻¹)_y v`. The metric coefficients,
the Christoffel symbols and the Riemann tensor are then given by the classical coordinate
formulas, using that coordinate vector fields commute.
-/

blocks.code:
noncomputable def metricCoord (x₀ : M) (y : E) : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  (innerSL ℝ).bilinearComp (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) I (extChartAt I x₀).symm y)
    (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) I (extChartAt I x₀).symm y)
blocks.docstring:
The metric coefficients of the Riemannian metric in the chart `e = extChartAt I x₀`, at the
coordinate point `y : E`: the bilinear form `(v, w) ↦ ⟪D(e⁻¹)_y v, D(e⁻¹)_y w⟫` on `E`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: RiemannianBundle / IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle give the inner product on each tangent space but no coordinate expression or connection.
justification.name: Eigenfunction.metricCoord
justification.why_needed: Metric coefficients of the Riemannian metric in a chart, the starting point for the coordinate computation of curvature.

blocks.name: metricCoord
blocks.text:
/-- The metric coefficients of the Riemannian metric in the chart `e = extChartAt I x₀`, at the
coordinate point `y : E`: the bilinear form `(v, w) ↦ ⟪D(e⁻¹)_y v, D(e⁻¹)_y w⟫` on `E`. -/
noncomputable def metricCoord (x₀ : M) (y : E) : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  (innerSL ℝ).bilinearComp (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) I (extChartAt I x₀).symm y)
    (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) I (extChartAt I x₀).symm y)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def christoffelFirst (x₀ : M) (y : E) (u v : E) : E →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  let D := fderiv ℝ (metricCoord I x₀) y
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (D u v + D v u - (D.flip u).flip v)
blocks.docstring:
The Christoffel symbols of the first kind in the chart `extChartAt I x₀`:
`christoffelFirst I x₀ y u v w = ½ (∂ᵤ g(v, w) + ∂ᵥ g(u, w) - ∂_w g(u, v))`, that is,
`g(∇ᵤ v, w)` for the coordinate vector fields `u`, `v`, `w`. Here `D = fderiv ℝ g y`, so that
`D u v w = ∂ᵤ g(v, w)` and `(D.flip u).flip v w = D w u v = ∂_w g(u, v)`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib (no affine connections); VectorField.mlieBracket exists but does not give a connection.
justification.name: Eigenfunction.christoffelFirst
justification.why_needed: Christoffel symbols of the first kind; Mathlib has no Levi-Civita connection.

blocks.name: christoffelFirst
blocks.text:
/-- The Christoffel symbols of the first kind in the chart `extChartAt I x₀`:
`christoffelFirst I x₀ y u v w = ½ (∂ᵤ g(v, w) + ∂ᵥ g(u, w) - ∂_w g(u, v))`, that is,
`g(∇ᵤ v, w)` for the coordinate vector fields `u`, `v`, `w`. Here `D = fderiv ℝ g y`, so that
`D u v w = ∂ᵤ g(v, w)` and `(D.flip u).flip v w = D w u v = ∂_w g(u, v)`. -/
noncomputable def christoffelFirst (x₀ : M) (y : E) (u v : E) : E →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  let D := fderiv ℝ (metricCoord I x₀) y
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (D u v + D v u - (D.flip u).flip v)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def christoffel (x₀ : M) (y : E) (u v : E) : E :=
  (metricCoord I x₀ y).inverse (christoffelFirst I x₀ y u v)
blocks.docstring:
The Christoffel symbols of the second kind in the chart `extChartAt I x₀`: the coordinate
vector `Γ(u, v) = ∇ᵤ v` characterised by `g(Γ(u, v), w) = christoffelFirst I x₀ y u v w` for all
`w`. It is obtained by inverting the metric coefficients; `ContinuousLinearMap.inverse` is the
genuine inverse because `metricCoord I x₀ y` is a linear isomorphism `E ≃ E*` for `y` in the
open target of the chart.

justification.closest_existing_considered: ContinuousLinearMap.inverse (used for raising the index); no connection exists in Mathlib.
justification.name: Eigenfunction.christoffel
justification.why_needed: Christoffel symbols of the second kind (∇ᵤv in coordinates), obtained by inverting the metric coefficients.

blocks.name: christoffel
blocks.text:
/-- The Christoffel symbols of the second kind in the chart `extChartAt I x₀`: the coordinate
vector `Γ(u, v) = ∇ᵤ v` characterised by `g(Γ(u, v), w) = christoffelFirst I x₀ y u v w` for all
`w`. It is obtained by inverting the metric coefficients; `ContinuousLinearMap.inverse` is the
genuine inverse because `metricCoord I x₀ y` is a linear isomorphism `E ≃ E*` for `y` in the
open target of the chart. -/
noncomputable def christoffel (x₀ : M) (y : E) (u v : E) : E :=
  (metricCoord I x₀ y).inverse (christoffelFirst I x₀ y u v)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def riemann (x₀ : M) (y : E) (u v w : E) : E :=
  fderiv ℝ (fun z ↦ christoffel I x₀ z v w) y u - fderiv ℝ (fun z ↦ christoffel I x₀ z u w) y v
    + christoffel I x₀ y u (christoffel I x₀ y v w) - christoffel I x₀ y v (christoffel I x₀ y u w)
blocks.docstring:
The Riemann curvature endomorphism `R(u, v) w = ∇ᵤ ∇ᵥ w - ∇ᵥ ∇ᵤ w` in the chart
`extChartAt I x₀`, for coordinate vector fields `u`, `v`, `w` (which commute):
`R(u, v) w = ∂ᵤ Γ(v, w) - ∂ᵥ Γ(u, w) + Γ(u, Γ(v, w)) - Γ(v, Γ(u, w))`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None (Mathlib has no curvature notions for Riemannian manifolds).
justification.name: Eigenfunction.riemann
justification.why_needed: Riemann curvature endomorphism in coordinates; absent from Mathlib.

blocks.name: riemann
blocks.text:
/-- The Riemann curvature endomorphism `R(u, v) w = ∇ᵤ ∇ᵥ w - ∇ᵥ ∇ᵤ w` in the chart
`extChartAt I x₀`, for coordinate vector fields `u`, `v`, `w` (which commute):
`R(u, v) w = ∂ᵤ Γ(v, w) - ∂ᵥ Γ(u, w) + Γ(u, Γ(v, w)) - Γ(v, Γ(u, w))`. -/
noncomputable def riemann (x₀ : M) (y : E) (u v w : E) : E :=
  fderiv ℝ (fun z ↦ christoffel I x₀ z v w) y u - fderiv ℝ (fun z ↦ christoffel I x₀ z u w) y v
    + christoffel I x₀ y u (christoffel I x₀ y v w) - christoffel I x₀ y v (christoffel I x₀ y u w)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def sectionalCurvature (x₀ : M) (u v : E) : ℝ :=
  let y := extChartAt I x₀ x₀
  let g := metricCoord I x₀ y
  g (riemann I x₀ y u v v) u / (g u u * g v v - (g u v) ^ 2)
blocks.docstring:
The sectional curvature of `M` at `x₀` along the plane spanned by the tangent vectors with
coordinates `u` and `v` in the chart `extChartAt I x₀`:
$$K(u, v) = \frac{g(R(u, v) v, u)}{g(u, u) g(v, v) - g(u, v)^2}.$$
It is only meaningful when `u` and `v` are linearly independent. With these conventions the
round sphere has `K = 1` and hyperbolic space has `K = -1`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (grep for curvature finds nothing relevant).
justification.name: Eigenfunction.sectionalCurvature
justification.why_needed: Sectional curvature at a point along a coordinate 2-plane; needed to express 'negatively curved'.

blocks.name: sectionalCurvature
blocks.text:
/-- The sectional curvature of `M` at `x₀` along the plane spanned by the tangent vectors with
coordinates `u` and `v` in the chart `extChartAt I x₀`:
$$K(u, v) = \frac{g(R(u, v) v, u)}{g(u, u) g(v, v) - g(u, v)^2}.$$
It is only meaningful when `u` and `v` are linearly independent. With these conventions the
round sphere has `K = 1` and hyperbolic space has `K = -1`. -/
noncomputable def sectionalCurvature (x₀ : M) (u v : E) : ℝ :=
  let y := extChartAt I x₀ x₀
  let g := metricCoord I x₀ y
  g (riemann I x₀ y u v v) u / (g u u * g v v - (g u v) ^ 2)

blocks.code:
def HasNegativeSectionalCurvature : Prop :=
  ∀ x₀ : M, ∀ u v : E, LinearIndependent ℝ ![u, v] → sectionalCurvature I x₀ u v < 0
blocks.docstring:
The Riemannian manifold `M` has strictly negative sectional curvature: at every point, the
sectional curvature of every tangent `2`-plane is negative.

justification.name: Eigenfunction.HasNegativeSectionalCurvature
justification.why_needed: The hypothesis 'strictly negative sectional curvature' of the conjecture.

blocks.name: HasNegativeSectionalCurvature
blocks.text:
variable (M) in
/-- The Riemannian manifold `M` has strictly negative sectional curvature: at every point, the
sectional curvature of every tangent `2`-plane is negative. -/
def HasNegativeSectionalCurvature : Prop :=
  ∀ x₀ : M, ∀ u v : E, LinearIndependent ℝ ![u, v] → sectionalCurvature I x₀ u v < 0
/- ### The conjecture -/

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 35 37 53 58 81]
theorem eigenfunction [IsManifold I ∞ M]
    [IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle I ∞ E (fun (x : M) ↦ TangentSpace I x)]
    [IsRiemannianManifold I M] [CompactSpace M] [ConnectedSpace M] [BoundarylessManifold I M]
    [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M]
    (hM : HasNegativeSectionalCurvature I M)
    (φ : ℕ → M → ℝ) (l : ℕ → ℝ) (hφ : ∀ k, IsLaplaceEigenfunction I (φ k) (l k))
    (hnorm : ∀ k, ∫ x, φ k x ^ 2 ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E)) = 1)
    (hl : Tendsto l atTop atTop) (f : C(M, ℝ)) :
    Tendsto (fun k ↦ ∫ x, f x * φ k x ^ 2 ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E))) atTop
      (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E)))) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Quantum unique ergodicity conjecture** (Rudnick–Sarnak). Let $M$ be a compact connected
smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary with strictly negative sectional curvature. Then for
every sequence $(\varphi_k)$ of $L^2$-normalised eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator,
$\Delta \varphi_k = \lambda_k \varphi_k$ with $\lambda_k \to \infty$, the measures
$|\varphi_k|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}$ converge weakly to the normalised Riemannian volume:
$$\int_M f \, |\varphi_k|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol} \longrightarrow
  \frac{1}{\mathrm{vol}(M)} \int_M f \, d\mathrm{vol}$$
for every continuous $f : M \to \mathbb{R}$. Here $d\mathrm{vol}$ is normalised to a probability
measure. Eigenfunctions are taken real-valued; since the Laplacian is a real operator, this is
equivalent to the formulation with complex-valued eigenfunctions. Connectedness is part of the
usual meaning of "manifold" here; without it the statement fails for eigenfunctions supported on
a single component.
blocks.name: eigenfunction
blocks.text:
/-- **Quantum unique ergodicity conjecture** (Rudnick–Sarnak). Let $M$ be a compact connected
smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary with strictly negative sectional curvature. Then for
every sequence $(\varphi_k)$ of $L^2$-normalised eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator,
$\Delta \varphi_k = \lambda_k \varphi_k$ with $\lambda_k \to \infty$, the measures
$|\varphi_k|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}$ converge weakly to the normalised Riemannian volume:
$$\int_M f \, |\varphi_k|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol} \longrightarrow
  \frac{1}{\mathrm{vol}(M)} \int_M f \, d\mathrm{vol}$$
for every continuous $f : M \to \mathbb{R}$. Here $d\mathrm{vol}$ is normalised to a probability
measure. Eigenfunctions are taken real-valued; since the Laplacian is a real operator, this is
equivalent to the formulation with complex-valued eigenfunctions. Connectedness is part of the
usual meaning of "manifold" here; without it the statement fails for eigenfunctions supported on
a single component. -/
@[category research open, AMS 35 37 53 58 81]
theorem eigenfunction [IsManifold I ∞ M]
    [IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle I ∞ E (fun (x : M) ↦ TangentSpace I x)]
    [IsRiemannianManifold I M] [CompactSpace M] [ConnectedSpace M] [BoundarylessManifold I M]
    [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M]
    (hM : HasNegativeSectionalCurvature I M)
    (φ : ℕ → M → ℝ) (l : ℕ → ℝ) (hφ : ∀ k, IsLaplaceEigenfunction I (φ k) (l k))
    (hnorm : ∀ k, ∫ x, φ k x ^ 2 ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E)) = 1)
    (hl : Tendsto l atTop atTop) (f : C(M, ℝ)) :
    Tendsto (fun k ↦ ∫ x, f x * φ k x ^ 2 ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E))) atTop
      (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E)))) := by
  sorry
/- ### Tests of the definitions -/

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 28]
theorem normalizedVolume_univ {M : Type*} [EMetricSpace M] [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M]
    (n : ℕ) (h0 : μH[n] (Set.univ : Set M) ≠ 0) (h1 : μH[n] (Set.univ : Set M) ≠ ⊤) :
    normalizedVolume M n Set.univ = 1 := by
  simp [normalizedVolume, ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel h0 h1]
blocks.docstring:
`normalizedVolume M n` is a probability measure when the `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of
`M` is finite and positive.

theorem isLaplaceEigenfunction_const [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M] (c : ℝ) :

/-- Constant functions are eigenfunctions of the Laplacian with eigenvalue `0`. -/

theorem isLaplaceEigenfunction_const [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M] (c : ℝ) :

claims.reviewer_why: c04 states the Rudnick–Sarnak configuration-space QUE exactly as the decomposition describes: compact connected boundaryless C^∞ Riemannian manifold (Mathlib's IsManifold/RiemannianBundle/IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle/IsRiemannianManifold), strictly negative sectional curvature, EVERY sequence of L²-normalised real Laplace eigenfunctions with eigenvalues → ∞, and ∫ f |φ_k|² dvol → ∫ f dvol/vol(M) for every continuous f. Its bespoke notions are built from existing primitives rather than abstract fields: volume = normalised n-dim Hausdorff measure of the Riemannian distance (a constant multiple of dvol; every use is scale-invariant), eigenfunction = smooth φ with the weak form ∫⟪∇φ,∇ψ⟫ = λ∫φψ for all smooth ψ (equivalent to −div∇φ = λφ by Green on a closed manifold; ∇ is the Riesz dual of mfderiv in the Riemannian tangent inner product — I verified with pp.explicit that the InnerProductSpace instance resolves via RiemannianBundle, not a Euclidean one), and sectional curvature computed in the preferred chart via metric coefficients → Christoffel symbols → Riemann tensor → K(u,v)=g(R(u,v)v,u)/(|u|²|v|²−g(u,v)²). I checked each formula by hand (flip semantics `(D.flip u).flip v w = D w u v` confirmed by rfl; Γ_{uv,w} = ½(∂ᵤg_{vw}+∂ᵥg_{uw}−∂_w g_{uv}); R(u,v)w = ∂ᵤΓ(v,w)−∂ᵥΓ(u,w)+Γ(u,Γ(v,w))−Γ(v,Γ(u,w)); on dx²+f(x)²dy² this gives K=−f''/f, so sphere K=1, hyperbolic K=−1) and the honesty of fderiv/ContinuousLinearMap.inverse on the open chart target of a boundaryless manifold. Preferred over c02/c05 (locally CAT(−κ) encodings, which I also judged correct) because it encodes 'strictly negative sectional curvature' literally and pointwise without going through Alexandrov's comparison theorem plus a compactness argument, and over c03 because the weak eigen-equation is more elementary than the Gray–Willmore mean-value expansion. Boundary cases: dim 0 makes λ_k→∞ impossible (vacuous), dim 1 (circle) makes the curvature hypothesis vacuous but the conclusion is true, so no false instance; connectedness is required (otherwise trivially false) and included. import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Quantum unique ergodicity for eigenfunctions of the Laplacian

The quantum unique ergodicity (QUE) conjecture of Rudnick and Sarnak concerns the distribution of
large-frequency eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on a compact Riemannian manifold
$M$ without boundary with strictly negative sectional curvature. It asserts that for *every*
sequence $(\varphi_k)$ of $L^2$-normalised eigenfunctions, $\Delta \varphi_k = \lambda_k \varphi_k$
with $\lambda_k \to \infty$, the probability measures $|\varphi_k|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}$ converge
weakly to the normalised Riemannian volume $d\mathrm{vol} / \mathrm{vol}(M)$. This strengthens the
quantum ergodicity theorem of Shnirelman, Zelditch and Colin de Verdière, which gives this
conclusion only along a subsequence of density one.

This file states the conjecture on the manifold $M$ itself (convergence of the measures
$|\varphi_k|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}$). The phase-space version, that Liouville measure is the only
quantum limit of the microlocal lifts on the unit cotangent bundle, is stronger and is not stated
here.

Mathlib has Riemannian manifolds (`IsRiemannianManifold`), but no Laplace–Beltrami operator,
Riemannian volume measure or curvature tensor. This file defines these notions from existing
primitives:

* the Riemannian volume is realised as the `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the Riemannian
  distance (`n = dim M`), which is a positive constant multiple of the Riemannian volume; the
  constant disappears after normalisation;
* eigenfunctions of the Laplacian are defined through the weak form of the eigenvalue equation
  $\int_M \langle \nabla \varphi, \nabla \psi \rangle = \lambda \int_M \varphi \psi$ for all smooth
  $\psi$, which on a compact manifold without boundary is equivalent to
  $\Delta \varphi = \lambda \varphi$ for the non-negative Laplacian
  $\Delta = -\operatorname{div} \nabla$;
* the sectional curvature is computed from the Christoffel symbols of the metric coefficients in
  the preferred chart at each point.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Eigenfunction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/eigenfunction)
* [Wikipedia, Quantum ergodicity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_ergodicity)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [RS94] Z. Rudnick, P. Sarnak, *The behaviour of eigenstates of arithmetic hyperbolic
  manifolds*, Comm. Math. Phys. 161 (1994), 195–213.
* [Sa11] P. Sarnak, *Recent progress on the quantum unique ergodicity conjecture*,
  Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 48 (2011), 211–228.
-/

open Bundle MeasureTheory Filter Topology
open scoped Manifold ContDiff

namespace Eigenfunction

/-
Throughout, `M` is a Riemannian manifold modelled on a finite-dimensional real vector space `E`:
its tangent spaces carry inner products (`RiemannianBundle`), and its extended distance is the
Riemannian distance (`IsRiemannianManifold I M`).
-/

variable
  {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  {H : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H)
  {M : Type*} [EMetricSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
  [RiemannianBundle (fun (x : M) ↦ TangentSpace I x)]

local notation "⟪" x ", " y "⟫" => inner ℝ x y

/-- The tangent spaces of a manifold modelled on a finite-dimensional space are
finite-dimensional. -/
local instance (x : M) : FiniteDimensional ℝ (TangentSpace I x) :=
  inferInstanceAs (FiniteDimensional ℝ E)

/- ### Riemannian volume and the Laplace–Beltrami operator -/

/-- The normalised `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of an extended metric space `M`.

When `M` is a compact `n`-dimensional Riemannian manifold whose distance is the Riemannian
distance, the `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure is a positive constant multiple of the
Riemannian volume, so `normalizedVolume M n` is the normalised Riemannian volume
$d\mathrm{vol} / \mathrm{vol}(M)$. -/
noncomputable def normalizedVolume (M : Type*) [EMetricSpace M] [MeasurableSpace M]
    [BorelSpace M] (n : ℕ) : Measure M :=
  (μH[n] (Set.univ : Set M))⁻¹ • μH[n]

/-- The Riemannian gradient of a function `φ : M → ℝ` at `x`: the tangent vector at `x`
representing the differential `dφ_x` through the Riemannian inner product on `TangentSpace I x`.
-/
noncomputable def gradient (φ : M → ℝ) (x : M) : TangentSpace I x :=
  (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (TangentSpace I x)).symm (mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) φ x)

/-- `IsLaplaceEigenfunction I φ l` means that `φ : M → ℝ` is a smooth eigenfunction of the
Laplace–Beltrami operator with eigenvalue `l`, in weak form: for every smooth `ψ : M → ℝ`,
$$\int_M \langle \nabla \varphi, \nabla \psi \rangle \, d\mathrm{vol}
  = l \int_M \varphi \, \psi \, d\mathrm{vol}.$$
On a compact manifold without boundary, Green's formula shows that this is equivalent to
$\Delta \varphi = l \varphi$ for the non-negative Laplace–Beltrami operator
$\Delta = -\operatorname{div} \nabla$. Eigenfunctions of the Laplacian are smooth by elliptic
regularity, so requiring `φ` to be smooth loses no generality. -/
def IsLaplaceEigenfunction [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M] (φ : M → ℝ) (l : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ φ ∧ ∀ ψ : M → ℝ, ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ ψ →
    ∫ x, ⟪gradient I φ x, gradient I ψ x⟫ ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E)) =
      l * ∫ x, φ x * ψ x ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E))

/-
### Sectional curvature

The curvature at a point `x₀` is computed in the preferred chart `e = extChartAt I x₀`. A vector
`v : E` is identified with the coordinate vector field `y ↦ D(e⁻¹)_y v`. The metric coefficients,
the Christoffel symbols and the Riemann tensor are then given by the classical coordinate
formulas, using that coordinate vector fields commute.
-/

/-- The metric coefficients of the Riemannian metric in the chart `e = extChartAt I x₀`, at the
coordinate point `y : E`: the bilinear form `(v, w) ↦ ⟪D(e⁻¹)_y v, D(e⁻¹)_y w⟫` on `E`. -/
noncomputable def metricCoord (x₀ : M) (y : E) : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  (innerSL ℝ).bilinearComp (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) I (extChartAt I x₀).symm y)
    (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) I (extChartAt I x₀).symm y)

/-- The Christoffel symbols of the first kind in the chart `extChartAt I x₀`:
`christoffelFirst I x₀ y u v w = ½ (∂ᵤ g(v, w) + ∂ᵥ g(u, w) - ∂_w g(u, v))`, that is,
`g(∇ᵤ v, w)` for the coordinate vector fields `u`, `v`, `w`. Here `D = fderiv ℝ g y`, so that
`D u v w = ∂ᵤ g(v, w)` and `(D.flip u).flip v w = D w u v = ∂_w g(u, v)`. -/
noncomputable def christoffelFirst (x₀ : M) (y : E) (u v : E) : E →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  let D := fderiv ℝ (metricCoord I x₀) y
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (D u v + D v u - (D.flip u).flip v)

/-- The Christoffel symbols of the second kind in the chart `extChartAt I x₀`: the coordinate
vector `Γ(u, v) = ∇ᵤ v` characterised by `g(Γ(u, v), w) = christoffelFirst I x₀ y u v w` for all
`w`. It is obtained by inverting the metric coefficients; `ContinuousLinearMap.inverse` is the
genuine inverse because `metricCoord I x₀ y` is a linear isomorphism `E ≃ E*` for `y` in the
open target of the chart. -/
noncomputable def christoffel (x₀ : M) (y : E) (u v : E) : E :=
  (metricCoord I x₀ y).inverse (christoffelFirst I x₀ y u v)

/-- The Riemann curvature endomorphism `R(u, v) w = ∇ᵤ ∇ᵥ w - ∇ᵥ ∇ᵤ w` in the chart
`extChartAt I x₀`, for coordinate vector fields `u`, `v`, `w` (which commute):
`R(u, v) w = ∂ᵤ Γ(v, w) - ∂ᵥ Γ(u, w) + Γ(u, Γ(v, w)) - Γ(v, Γ(u, w))`. -/
noncomputable def riemann (x₀ : M) (y : E) (u v w : E) : E :=
  fderiv ℝ (fun z ↦ christoffel I x₀ z v w) y u - fderiv ℝ (fun z ↦ christoffel I x₀ z u w) y v
    + christoffel I x₀ y u (christoffel I x₀ y v w) - christoffel I x₀ y v (christoffel I x₀ y u w)

/-- The sectional curvature of `M` at `x₀` along the plane spanned by the tangent vectors with
coordinates `u` and `v` in the chart `extChartAt I x₀`:
$$K(u, v) = \frac{g(R(u, v) v, u)}{g(u, u) g(v, v) - g(u, v)^2}.$$
It is only meaningful when `u` and `v` are linearly independent. With these conventions the
round sphere has `K = 1` and hyperbolic space has `K = -1`. -/
noncomputable def sectionalCurvature (x₀ : M) (u v : E) : ℝ :=
  let y := extChartAt I x₀ x₀
  let g := metricCoord I x₀ y
  g (riemann I x₀ y u v v) u / (g u u * g v v - (g u v) ^ 2)

variable (M) in
/-- The Riemannian manifold `M` has strictly negative sectional curvature: at every point, the
sectional curvature of every tangent `2`-plane is negative. -/
def HasNegativeSectionalCurvature : Prop :=
  ∀ x₀ : M, ∀ u v : E, LinearIndependent ℝ ![u, v] → sectionalCurvature I x₀ u v < 0

/- ### The conjecture -/

/-- **Quantum unique ergodicity conjecture** (Rudnick–Sarnak). Let $M$ be a compact connected
smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary with strictly negative sectional curvature. Then for
every sequence $(\varphi_k)$ of $L^2$-normalised eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator,
$\Delta \varphi_k = \lambda_k \varphi_k$ with $\lambda_k \to \infty$, the measures
$|\varphi_k|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}$ converge weakly to the normalised Riemannian volume:
$$\int_M f \, |\varphi_k|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol} \longrightarrow
  \frac{1}{\mathrm{vol}(M)} \int_M f \, d\mathrm{vol}$$
for every continuous $f : M \to \mathbb{R}$. Here $d\mathrm{vol}$ is normalised to a probability
measure. Eigenfunctions are taken real-valued; since the Laplacian is a real operator, this is
equivalent to the formulation with complex-valued eigenfunctions. Connectedness is part of the
usual meaning of "manifold" here; without it the statement fails for eigenfunctions supported on
a single component. -/
@[category research open, AMS 35 37 53 58 81]
theorem eigenfunction [IsManifold I ∞ M]
    [IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle I ∞ E (fun (x : M) ↦ TangentSpace I x)]
    [IsRiemannianManifold I M] [CompactSpace M] [ConnectedSpace M] [BoundarylessManifold I M]
    [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M]
    (hM : HasNegativeSectionalCurvature I M)
    (φ : ℕ → M → ℝ) (l : ℕ → ℝ) (hφ : ∀ k, IsLaplaceEigenfunction I (φ k) (l k))
    (hnorm : ∀ k, ∫ x, φ k x ^ 2 ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E)) = 1)
    (hl : Tendsto l atTop atTop) (f : C(M, ℝ)) :
    Tendsto (fun k ↦ ∫ x, f x * φ k x ^ 2 ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E))) atTop
      (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E)))) := by
  sorry

/- ### Tests of the definitions -/

/-- `normalizedVolume M n` is a probability measure when the `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of
`M` is finite and positive. -/
@[category test, AMS 28]
theorem normalizedVolume_univ {M : Type*} [EMetricSpace M] [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M]
    (n : ℕ) (h0 : μH[n] (Set.univ : Set M) ≠ 0) (h1 : μH[n] (Set.univ : Set M) ≠ ⊤) :
    normalizedVolume M n Set.univ = 1 := by
  simp [normalizedVolume, ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel h0 h1]

/-- The gradient of a constant function vanishes. -/
@[category test, AMS 53 58]
theorem gradient_const (c : ℝ) (x : M) : gradient I (fun _ ↦ c) x = 0 := by
  simp [gradient]

/-- Constant functions are eigenfunctions of the Laplacian with eigenvalue `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 35 58]
theorem isLaplaceEigenfunction_const [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M] (c : ℝ) :
    IsLaplaceEigenfunction I (fun _ : M ↦ c) 0 := by
  refine ⟨contMDiff_const, fun ψ _ ↦ ?_⟩
  simp [gradient_const]

section VectorSpace

variable {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F]

/-- For an inner product space with its canonical Riemannian metric, the metric coefficients in
the (identity) chart are the inner product. -/
@[category test, AMS 53]
theorem metricCoord_vectorSpace (x₀ y : F) : metricCoord 𝓘(ℝ, F) x₀ y = innerSL ℝ := by
  ext v w
  simp [metricCoord, mfderiv_id]
  rfl

/-- An inner product space with its canonical Riemannian metric is flat. -/
@[category test, AMS 53]
theorem sectionalCurvature_vectorSpace (x₀ u v : F) :
    sectionalCurvature 𝓘(ℝ, F) x₀ u v = 0 := by
  have hg : metricCoord 𝓘(ℝ, F) x₀ = fun _ ↦ innerSL ℝ := funext (metricCoord_vectorSpace x₀)
  have hΓ : christoffel 𝓘(ℝ, F) x₀ = fun _ _ _ ↦ 0 := by
    funext y u v
    have h0 : fderiv ℝ (metricCoord 𝓘(ℝ, F) x₀) y = 0 := by
      rw [hg]
      exact congrFun (fderiv_fun_const (𝕜 := ℝ) (E := F) (innerSL ℝ (E := F))) y
    simp [christoffel, christoffelFirst, h0]
  simp [sectionalCurvature, riemann, hΓ]

end VectorSpace

end Eigenfunction

items: Statement scope: the list entry is terse; following the decomposition table and Rudnick–Sarnak, the configuration-space QUE is formalised: for EVERY sequence (not a density-one subsequence) of L²-normalised Laplace eigenfunctions φ_k with eigenvalues λ_k → ∞, ∫ f |φ_k|² dvol → ∫ f dvol (vol normalised) for every continuous f : M → ℝ (weak convergence of probability measures on the compact metric space M).

Manifold hypotheses: `[IsManifold I ∞ M]` (smooth), `[RiemannianBundle]` + `[IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle I ∞ E ..]` (smooth Riemannian metric), `[IsRiemannianManifold I M]` (the EMetric distance on M is the Riemannian distance), `[CompactSpace M]`, `[BoundarylessManifold I M]`, `[FiniteDimensional ℝ E]`. `[ConnectedSpace M]` is added: for a disconnected manifold QUE fails trivially (eigenfunctions supported on one component), and 'a negatively curved manifold' in this context is connected. No lower bound on the dimension is imposed; in dimension ≤ 1 the curvature hypothesis is vacuous but the conclusion is (trivially) true for the circle and vacuous for a point, so no false instance is introduced.

Riemannian volume: `normalizedVolume M n` is the n-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the Riemannian distance (n = finrank ℝ E = dim M) divided by its total mass. On a Riemannian manifold the n-dimensional Hausdorff measure is a positive dimensional constant times the Riemannian volume (Mathlib's `μH` has no normalising constant), so after normalisation it is exactly dvol / vol(M). Both the L² normalisation and the eigenvalue equation are invariant under scaling the measure, so using the normalised measure throughout is harmless.

Laplace eigenfunctions: `IsLaplaceEigenfunction I φ l` requires φ smooth and ∫⟪∇φ,∇ψ⟫ dvol = l ∫ φ ψ dvol for all smooth ψ, with ∇ the Riemannian gradient (Riesz representative of `mfderiv` in the tangent space with its Riemannian inner product, via `InnerProductSpace.toDual`). On a compact boundaryless manifold, Green's formula makes this equivalent to Δφ = lφ for Δ = -div grad ≥ 0; smoothness is automatic for eigenfunctions (elliptic regularity), so the smoothness requirement loses nothing. Eigenvalues are therefore ≥ 0 and 'large frequency' is `Tendsto l atTop atTop`.

Real-valued eigenfunctions are used. Since Δ is a real operator, the complex-valued formulation is equivalent (|u+iv|² = u²+v² with u, v real eigenfunctions of the same eigenvalue; a subsequence argument gives the same weak limit).

Sectional curvature: computed in the preferred chart e = extChartAt I x₀ at each point x₀. `metricCoord I x₀ y v w = ⟪D(e⁻¹)_y v, D(e⁻¹)_y w⟫` are the metric coefficients (coordinate vector fields commute, so the classical formulas apply); `christoffelFirst` is ½(∂ᵤg(v,w)+∂ᵥg(u,w)-∂_w g(u,v)) = g(∇ᵤv,w); `christoffel` raises the index with `ContinuousLinearMap.inverse` (a genuine inverse on the open chart target where g is positive definite); `riemann` is R(u,v)w = ∂ᵤΓ(v,w) - ∂ᵥΓ(u,w) + Γ(u,Γ(v,w)) - Γ(v,Γ(u,w)) (convention R(X,Y)Z = ∇_X∇_Y Z - ∇_Y∇_X Z - ∇_[X,Y]Z); `sectionalCurvature` is g(R(u,v)v,u)/(g(u,u)g(v,v)-g(u,v)²), the convention under which the round sphere has K > 0 (checked by hand on warped metrics dx² + f(x)²dy², giving K = -f''/f). `HasNegativeSectionalCurvature I M` asks K < 0 at every point for all linearly independent u, v; on a compact manifold this equals K ≤ -ε. The `fderiv`s are honest because for a boundaryless manifold the chart target is a neighbourhood of every coordinate point and all ingredients are smooth there.
A `local instance` `FiniteDimensional ℝ (TangentSpace I x)` (from `FiniteDimensional ℝ E`) is used so that `InnerProductSpace.toDual` applies to tangent spaces.

The bespoke definitions are generic Riemannian-geometry notions and would ideally live in `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/`; they are kept in the problem file only because the task restricts output to the single candidate file.

Basic API tests are included and proved: `normalizedVolume` is a probability measure when the Hausdorff measure is finite and positive; constants are eigenfunctions with eigenvalue 0; an inner product space with its canonical metric has metric coefficients equal to the inner product and zero sectional curvature.

reviewer_notes: The Wikipedia list entry is a bare title; the decomposition table fixes the precise reading as the Rudnick–Sarnak QUE conjecture in configuration space (|φ_j|² dvol → dvol/vol(M) for every sequence with λ_j → ∞). All four formalising candidates (c02–c05) and I agree that the phase-space version (Liouville measure is the only quantum limit of microlocal lifts on S*M) is formally STRONGER than the base version, not 'equivalent' as the table notes say; the base version is what Rudnick–Sarnak state on M and what the entry's wording ('distribution of eigenfunctions') refers to, so it is what the final file states, with the docstring saying so explicitly. Omission verdicts: c01, c06, c07, c08 bailed out with 'missing primitives' (no Laplace–Beltrami, sectional curvature, or Riemannian volume in Mathlib). Their premise that abstract unconstrained fields would be unfaithful is correct, but c02–c05 showed the missing notions can be defined faithfully from existing primitives (Hausdorff measure of the Riemannian distance, mfderiv + RiemannianBundle inner product, extChartAt coordinate formulas or CAT(−κ) comparison), so the bail-outs are not convincing. All four written candidates were judged faithful; c04 chosen as explained per slot. Residual risk lies in the bespoke definitions being mathematically what they claim (checked by hand, plus the flat-space test theorems in the file), not in the logical shape of the statement. Real-valued eigenfunctions are used; the complex-valued formulation is equivalent (real/imaginary parts are eigenfunctions with the same eigenvalue).
